system.name: Tooth
system.one_liner: a control module that fine-tunes forward error correction to balance video QoE and redundancy cost in cloud gaming streaming

components.name: Tooth
components.role: pivotal control module positioned between Video Codec and FEC Codec, tuning fine-grained FEC to balance QoE and redundancy cost

components.name: FEC Codec
components.role: applies forward error correction coding to the video stream

components.name: Data Sender
components.role: transmits the encoded, FEC-protected data over the network

components.name: Network Monitor
components.role: monitors network conditions and supplies feedback to Tooth

components.name: Internet
components.role: network connecting the cloud game server to player devices

components.name: Player Devices
components.role: client devices (phones, laptop) receiving and rendering the streamed game

content.key_idea: Tooth sits between a cloud game server's Video Codec and FEC Codec, using network-monitor feedback to fine-tune forward error correction per session before the data sender streams protected video over the Internet to multiple player devices.
content.reading_order: Left to right: inside the Cloud Game Server, video flows through Video Codec, Tooth, FEC Codec and Data Sender; the stream then crosses the Internet to three Player Devices.

summary: Tooth is a fine-grained forward-error-correction (FEC) control module for cloud gaming that balances video QoE against redundancy cost. Figure 15 shows its implementation as a pipeline inside a Cloud Game Server: a Video Codec encodes the game stream, which passes through Tooth -- highlighted in red as the pivotal control module positioned between Video Codec and FEC Codec -- before the FEC Codec applies error-correction coding and a Data Sender transmits the result. A Network Monitor alongside Tooth supplies the network-condition feedback Tooth uses to tune its per-session FEC decisions. The protected stream then crosses the Internet (drawn as a cloud with differently colored lines) to reach three Player Devices -- a phone, a laptop, and another handheld device -- each shown rendering the live game. The figure is a clean, icon-heavy illustration with realistic device/server artwork and very little text, leaning on recognizable pictures instead of abstract boxes.
summary_zh: 图15展示Tooth在云游戏服务器中的实现：位于Video Codec与FEC Codec之间，结合Network Monitor反馈调节FEC，经Data Sender通过互联网传给多台玩家设备。
notes: The retrieved text is one sentence plus a truncated continuation ('Tooth acquires the receipt'), so the Network Monitor's exact feed direction and the Data Sender/Internet/Player Devices connections are read from the figure alone. layout-proposal: pipeline-into-fanout — a server-side codec pipeline (Video Codec, Tooth, FEC Codec, Data Sender) feeds a single Internet hub that fans out to multiple identical Player Device spokes; host-device captures the server/client split but not the internal pipeline or the multi-device fanout.
